task.title: roman-to-numeral
task.statement: The roman package exposes is_roman_numeral (already implemented) and a stub to_roman(n). Implement to_roman(n) so that it converts an integer n in the range 1..3999 inclusive to its standard Roman numeral string using subtractive notation (4='IV', 9='IX', 40='XL', 90='XC', 400='CD', 900='CM'). Return a str. Raise ValueError when n is an int outside 1..3999. Raise TypeError when n is not an int (bool counts as non-int for this task is not required; treat only real ints as valid). Do not change is_roman_numeral or the tests.

classifications.rationale: The contract states to raise TypeError for non-integer inputs, including bool. However, it does not explicitly specify whether other subclasses of int (like a user-defined MyInt) should be accepted or rejected. The candidate implementation rejects all subclasses by checking `type(n) is not int`, while the test expects subclasses to be accepted. Reasonable interpretations differ: one could argue 'int' means isinstance(n, int) (accepting subclasses), or that 'int' means the exact built-in type (rejecting subclasses, as the contract explicitly excludes bool which is a subclass). The contract is ambiguous on this point.
classifications.contract_basis: Contract: 'Raise TypeError for non-integer inputs (including bool, float, str, None, list, etc.)' and original note 'treat only real ints as valid'.
